excerpt: MMC 2450: Fall 25 1 MMC 2450: Data Literacy for Communicators Tuesdays, 3:00pm-3:50pm MAT 0118 Office Hours: Tuesdays: 1:00pm-3:00pm PROFESSOR OFFICE Frank Waddell, Ph.D. frank.waddell@ufl.edu 3067 Weimer Hall REQUIRED RESOURCES/READINGS All readings will be posted to Canvas or available via UF library access COURSE DESCRIPTION Data Literacy for Communicators (MMC 2450) introduces students to the fundamentals of data interpretation in the context of journalism. Topics to be covered include central tendency, dispersion, percentages, probability, sampling, causation, correlation, and methodology, among other topics. COURSE OBJECTIVES Course objectives include (1) familiarity with key concepts related to data literacy, (2) the ability to interpret data-focused journalism, and (3) the development of critical thinking skills for critiquing data-based claims. GRADING Class Attendance/Participation: 20% Numeracy critique: 20% Midterm exam: 30% Final exam: 30% Grading scale: A, 100-93; A-, 92-90; B+, 89-87; B, 86-84; B-, 83-80; C+, 79-77; C, 76-74; C-, 73-70; D+, 69-67; D, 66-64; D-, 63-60; E, 59 and below MMC 2450: Fall 25 2 Information on current UF grading policies can be found at: https://catalog.ufl.edu/ugrad/current/regulations/info/grades.aspx ASSIGNMENTS Class attendance/participation (20%): Students are required to come to class each week for the full class session. Grading for class attendance/participation will be based on arriving to class on time each week, attending the entire class session and participating in class discussion. If you need to miss class for illness or an emergency, please contact me in advance to ensure the absence is excused. Absences without a valid excuse, arriving to class late, leaving class early or not participating during class discussions will lead to a lower grade for class attendance/participation. Exams (60%): Two exams will be completed during the semester: one midterm exam and one final exam. Each exam is worth 20% of your final grade. The exams will cover key course content covered during lecture and from class readings. The format and timing of the exam will be summarized during the semester. Numeracy critique (20%): Students will find and critique an example of journalistic writing that uses data-focused reporting. The assignment will require students to explain the numeracy principles that were used and offer a critique of whether the writing accurately conveyed the information that was summarized. The assignment will be no more than 2 double-spaced pages. More directions will be provided during the course of the semester. LATE WORK POLICY One letter grade (-10 points) will be deducted per day for work submitted past the assignment’s deadline. If an exam is missed, official documentation must be provided for the absence, with a makeup test scheduled within one week of the original examination. If students anticipate that they will be unable to meet a deadline due to university documented issues (e.g., health condition, death in family), please contact me as soon as possible to arrange an extension. In general, I am quite willing to work with students when issues arise that prevent you from submitting work on time. HONOR CODE POLICY This class strictly adheres to the UF honor code.
